title: Unit summary and review exercise
competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 3.

keywords.def: A relationship in which both sides affect each other.
Resources that can replace themselves naturally after use.
Resources that cannot be replaced once used.
The number of people a region can support without environmental degradation.

en.text: Humans and the environment affect each other. Population and resources depend on each other: over, under or optimum population. Resources are renewable or non-renewable. In Ethiopia, population pressure, resettlement, agricultural expansion and rapid urbanization affect resources.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Climate, relief and soil influence how people live.
People can modify their environment with skill, knowledge and experience.
Population and resources have a strong relationship with one another.
Natural resources are renewable or non-renewable.
table: Replace themselves: air, water, sunlight, wind, forest
Cannot be replaced: oil, natural gas, coal
Population pressure, resettlement, agricultural expansion, rapid urbanization

Population grows → forests grow → more rain

screens.ans: Population grows → more farmland needed → forests cleared → biodiversity declines
screens.why: Population pressure and agricultural expansion clear forests, and the book lists decline of biodiversity as a consequence.

notes.text: The chapter test draws 20 questions round-robin from the five section tests (3.1, 3.2, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.4), rotating levels, 25 minutes, no clues.
The glossary defines non-renewable resources as "resources that can replace themselves"; this is an error. The lesson uses p.80 and the summary: they cannot be replaced once used.

Review Exercise IV 1–4 are in the section lessons (3.4, 3.3.2, ★). Section V short answers are covered by the idea explanations and section items; V 5 (sustainable economy) is not taught in the book and is left out.
The Check List (p.92) is a self-assessment and is not turned into questions.
